```text
import { createBundleWorkflow } from "@medusajs/core-flows"
import { medusaIntegrationTestRunner } from "@medusajs/test-utils"
import {
  ContainerRegistrationKeys,
  ProductStatus,
} from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import {
  adminHeaders,
  createAdminUser,
  generatePublishableKey,
  generateStoreHeaders,
} from "../../../../helpers/create-admin-user"

jest.setTimeout(100000)

/**
 * Integration tests for issue #112 "Add API to create and manage product
 * bundles" (part 1 of #101). Each `describe` below is named after the
 * acceptance criterion (AC) it covers, so the issue can be checked off
 * against this file.
 *
 * Model under test: a bundle is a product with ONE variant that has its own
 * prices and is linked (inventory kit) to the component inventory items. The
 * component list is stored in product.metadata.bundle.
 */
medusaIntegrationTestRunner({
  testSuite: ({ dbConnection, getContainer, api }) => {
    let appContainer
    let storeHeaders
    let shippingProfile
    let salesChannel
    let stockLocation
    let category
    let region
    let shippingOption

    // Makes the "failing hook" test (AC 8) possible. Hooks can't be removed once
    // registered, so the handler is registered once and switched on and off.
    let failBundleCreatedHook = false

    // Counter so every helper call gets unique SKUs / titles / handles.
    let seq = 0

    /**
     * Creates a normal product with one variant that tracks inventory, has
     * `stocked` units in the shared stock location and an optional
     * `required_quantity` on its inventory item. This is what a bundle
     * component looks like.
     */
    const createComponent = async (
      title: string,
      stocked: number,
      requiredQuantity = 1
    ) => {
      seq++
      const inventoryItem = (
        await api.post(
          "/admin/inventory-items",
          { sku: `${title}-sku-${seq}` },
          adminHeaders
        )
      ).data.inventory_item

      await api.post(
        `/admin/inventory-items/${inventoryItem.id}/location-levels`,
        { location_id: stockLocation.id, stocked_quantity: stocked },
        adminHeaders
      )

      const product = (
        await api.post(
          "/admin/products",
          {
            title: `${title} ${seq}`,
            status: ProductStatus.PUBLISHED,
            shipping_profile_id: shippingProfile.id,
            sales_channels: [{ id: salesChannel.id }],
            options: [{ title: "Default", values: ["Default"] }],
            variants: [
              {
                title: `${title} variant`,
                options: { Default: "Default" },
                manage_inventory: true,
                inventory_items: [
                  {
                    inventory_item_id: inventoryItem.id,
                    required_quantity: requiredQuantity,
                  },
                ],
                // Component prices are deliberately different from the bundle
                // price (AC 10).
                prices: [{ currency_code: "usd", amount: 500 }],
              },
            ],
          },
          adminHeaders
        )
      ).data.product

      return { product, variant: product.variants[0], inventoryItem }
    }

    /**
     * The "Camera kit" from the issue: 1x camera, 1x lens, 1x bag at
     * $899 / EUR 849. Returns the components too so tests can inspect them.
     */
    const createCameraKitParts = async (stock = { camera: 10, lens: 10, bag: 10 }) => ({
      camera: await createComponent("Camera", stock.camera),
      lens: await createComponent("Lens", stock.lens),
      bag: await createComponent("Bag", stock.bag),
    })

    const bundleBody = (parts, overrides: Record<string, unknown> = {}) => {
      seq++
      return {
        title: `Camera kit ${seq}`,
        description: "Everything to start shooting",
        status: ProductStatus.PUBLISHED,
        images: [{ url: "https://example.com/camera-kit.png" }],
        categories: [{ id: category.id }],
        shipping_profile_id: shippingProfile.id,
        sales_channels: [{ id: salesChannel.id }],
        components: [
          { variant_id: parts.camera.variant.id, quantity: 1 },
          { variant_id: parts.lens.variant.id, quantity: 1 },
          { variant_id: parts.bag.variant.id, quantity: 1 },
        ],
        prices: [
          { currency_code: "usd", amount: 899 },
          { currency_code: "eur", amount: 849 },
        ],
        ...overrides,
      }
    }
```

```typescript
import { medusaIntegrationTestRunner } from "@medusajs/test-utils"
import { ProductStatus, RuleOperator } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import {
  adminHeaders,
  createAdminUser,
  generatePublishableKey,
  generateStoreHeaders,
} from "../../../../helpers/create-admin-user"
import { createAuthenticatedCustomer } from "../../../../modules/helpers/create-authenticated-customer"

jest.setTimeout(200000)

/**
 * Integration tests for issue #113 "Handle bundles at checkout and allow
 * returning a single item from a bundle" (part 2 of #101). Each `describe` is
 * named after the acceptance criterion (AC) it covers.
 *
 * The scenario is the issue's: a Camera kit made of a camera (normally $800),
 * a lens ($300) and a bag ($100), sold for $1,000. Its shares are $666.67,
 * $250.00 and $83.33.
 */
medusaIntegrationTestRunner({
  testSuite: ({ dbConnection, getContainer, api }) => {
    let storeHeaders
    let customerHeaders
    let otherCustomerHeaders
    let shippingProfile
    let salesChannel
    let stockLocation
    let region
    let shippingOption
    let returnShippingOption

    let seq = 0

    const createComponent = async (title: string, price: number, stocked: number) => {
      seq++
      const inventoryItem = (
        await api.post("/admin/inventory-items", { sku: `${title}-${seq}` }, adminHeaders)
      ).data.inventory_item

      await api.post(
        `/admin/inventory-items/${inventoryItem.id}/location-levels`,
        { location_id: stockLocation.id, stocked_quantity: stocked },
        adminHeaders
      )

      const product = (
        await api.post(
          "/admin/products",
          {
            title,
            status: ProductStatus.PUBLISHED,
            shipping_profile_id: shippingProfile.id,
            sales_channels: [{ id: salesChannel.id }],
            options: [{ title: "Default", values: ["Default"] }],
            variants: [
              {
                title: `${title} ${seq}`,
                options: { Default: "Default" },
                manage_inventory: true,
                inventory_items: [
                  { inventory_item_id: inventoryItem.id, required_quantity: 1 },
                ],
                prices: [{ currency_code: "usd", amount: price }],
              },
            ],
          },
          adminHeaders
        )
      ).data.product

      return { product, variant: product.variants[0], inventoryItem }
    }

    /**
     * The issue's Camera kit, with `stock` units of each component.
     */
    const createCameraKit = async (
      stock = { camera: 10, lens: 10, bag: 10 },
      price = 1000
    ) => {
      const camera = await createComponent("Camera body", 800, stock.camera)
      const lens = await createComponent("Lens", 300, stock.lens)
      const bag = await createComponent("Bag", 100, stock.bag)

      const bundle = (
        await api.post(
          "/admin/bundles",
          {
            title: `Camera kit`,
            status: ProductStatus.PUBLISHED,
            shipping_profile_id: shippingProfile.id,
            sales_channels: [{ id: salesChannel.id }],
            components: [
              { variant_id: camera.variant.id, quantity: 1 },
              { variant_id: lens.variant.id, quantity: 1 },
              { variant_id: bag.variant.id, quantity: 1 },
            ],
            prices: [{ currency_code: "usd", amount: price }],
          },
          adminHeaders
        )
      ).data.product

      return { camera, lens, bag, bundle, variant: bundle.variants[0] }
    }

    const createCart = async (
      items: { variant_id: string; quantity: number }[],
      headers = customerHeaders
    ) => {
      const cart = (
        await api.post(
          "/store/carts",
          {
            email: "tony@stark-industries.com",
            currency_code: "usd",
            sales_channel_id: salesChannel.id,
            region_id: region.id,
            shipping_address: {
              address_1: "1 Main St",
              city: "SF",
              country_code: "us",
              province: "CA",
              postal_code: "94016",
            },
            items,
          },
          headers
        )
      ).data.cart

      await api.post(
        `/store/carts/${cart.id}/shipping-methods`,
        { option_id: shippingOption.id },
        headers
      )

      const paymentCollection = (
        await api.post("/store/payment-collections", { cart_id: cart.id }, headers)
      ).data.payment_collection

      await api.post(
        `/store/payment-collections/${paymentCollection.id}/payment-sessions`,
        { provider_id: "pp_system_default" },
        headers
      )

      return cart
    }

    const completeCart = async (cartId: string, headers = customerHeaders) =>
      (await api.post(`/store/carts/${cartId}/complete`, {}, headers)).data

    const placeOrder = async (variantId: string, quantity = 1) => {
      const cart = await createCart([{ variant_id: variantId, quantity }])
      const { order } = await completeCart(cart.id)
      return order
    }

    const getOrder = async (orderId: string) =>
      (
        await api.get(
          `/admin/orders/${orderId}?fields=*items,items.metadata,*summary`,
          adminHeaders
        )
      ).data.order

    const fulfillAll = async (orderId: string) => {
      const order = await getOrder(orderId)
      await api.post(
        `/admin/orders/${orderId}/fulfillments`,
        {
          location_id: stockLocation.id,
          items: order.items.map((item) => ({ id: item.id, quantity: item.quantity })),
        },
        adminHeaders
      )
      return await getOrder(orderId)
    }

    const getLevel = async (inventoryItemId: string) =>
      (
        await api.get(
          `/admin/inventory-items/${inventoryItemId}/location-levels`,
          adminHeaders
        )
      ).data.inventory_levels.find((level) => level.location_id === stockLocation.id)

    const setStock = async (inventoryItemId: string, stocked: number) =>
      api.post(
        `/admin/inventory-items/${inventoryItemId}/location-levels/${stockLocation.id}`,
        { stocked_quantity: stocked },
        adminHeaders
      )

    const storeReturn = async (orderId: string, items: any[], headers = customerHeaders) =>
      api.post(
        "/store/returns",
        {
          order_id: orderId,
          items,
          return_shipping: { option_id: returnShippingOption.id, price: 0 },
        },
        headers
      )

    const pendingDifference = async (orderId: string) =>
      Number((await getOrder(orderId)).summary.pending_difference)

    beforeAll(async () => {
      const container = getContainer()
      await createAdminUser(dbConnection, adminHeaders, container)

      const publishableKey = await generatePublishableKey(container)
      storeHeaders = generateStoreHeaders({ publishableKey })

      const customer = await createAuthenticatedCustomer(api, storeHeaders, {
        email: "tony@stark-industries.com",
      })
      customerHeaders = {
        headers: { ...storeHeaders.headers, authorization: `Bearer ${customer.jwt}` },
      }
      const otherCustomer = await createAuthenticatedCustomer(api, storeHeaders, {
        email: "steve@rogers.com",
      })
      otherCustomerHeaders = {
        headers: {
          ...storeHeaders.headers,
          authorization: `Bearer ${otherCustomer.jwt}`,
        },
      }

      shippingProfile = (
        await api.post(
          "/admin/shipping-profiles",
          { name: "default", type: "default" },
          adminHeaders
        )
      ).data.shipping_profile

      region = (
        await api.post(
          "/admin/regions",
          { name: "US", currency_code: "usd", countries: ["us"] },
          adminHeaders
        )
      ).data.region

      salesChannel = (
        await api.post("/admin/sales-channels", { name: "Webshop" }, adminHeaders)
      ).data.sales_channel

      await api.post(
        `/admin/api-keys/${publishableKey.id}/sales-channels`,
        { add: [salesChannel.id] },
        adminHeaders
      )

      stockLocation = (
        await api.post("/admin/stock-locations", { name: "Warehouse" }, adminHeaders)
      ).data.stock_location

      await api.post(
        `/admin/stock-locations/${stockLocation.id}/sales-channels`,
        { add: [salesChannel.id] },
        adminHeaders
      )

      const fulfillmentSets = (
        await api.post(
          `/admin/stock-locations/${stockLocation.id}/fulfillment-sets?fields=*fulfillment_sets`,
          { name: "Bundle-fulfillment", type: "shipping" },
          adminHeaders
        )
      ).data.stock_location.fulfillment_sets

      const fulfillmentSet = (
        await api.post(
          `/admin/fulfillment-sets/${fulfillmentSets[0].id}/service-zones`,
          { name: "Zone", geo_zones: [{ type: "country", country_code: "us" }] },
          adminHeaders
        )
      ).data.fulfillment_set

      await api.post(
        `/admin/stock-locations/${stockLocation.id}/fulfillment-providers`,
        { add: ["manual_test-provider"] },
        adminHeaders
      )

      const optionBody = (name: string, rules: any[]) => ({
        name,
        service_zone_id: fulfillmentSet.service_zones[0].id,
        shipping_profile_id: shippingProfile.id,
        provider_id: "manual_test-provider",
        price_type: "flat",
        type: { label: "Std", description: "Std", code: "std" },
        prices: [{ currency_code: "usd", amount: 0 }],
        rules,
      })

      shippingOption = (
        await api.post("/admin/shipping-options", optionBody("Shipping", []), adminHeaders)
      ).data.shipping_option

      returnShippingOption = (
        await api.post(
          "/admin/shipping-options",
          optionBody("Return shipping", [
            { operator: RuleOperator.EQ, attribute: "is_return", value: "true" },
          ]),
          adminHeaders
        )
      ).data.shipping_option
    })

    describe("AC 1-3: the out-of-stock error names the product", () => {
      it("names the bundle component that is out of stock at checkout (AC 1)", async () => {
        const kit = await createCameraKit()
        const cart = await createCart([{ variant_id: kit.variant.id, quantity: 1 }])

        // The lens sells out before the shopper checks out.
        await setStock(kit.lens.inventoryItem.id, 0)

        const result = await completeCart(cart.id)

        expect(result.type).toEqual("cart")
        expect(result.error.message).toEqual("Camera kit: Lens is out of stock.")
      })

      it("names every out-of-stock component (AC 2)", async () => {
        const kit = await createCameraKit()
        const cart = await createCart([{ variant_id: kit.variant.id, quantity: 1 }])

        await setStock(kit.lens.inventoryItem.id, 0)
        await setStock(kit.bag.inventoryItem.id, 0)

        const result = await completeCart(cart.id)

        expect(result.error.message).toEqual(
          "Camera kit: Lens, Bag are out of stock."
        )
      })

      it("names the component when adding the bundle to the cart", async () => {
        const kit = await createCameraKit({ camera: 10, lens: 0, bag: 10 })

        const error = await api
          .post(
            "/store/carts",
            {
              currency_code: "usd",
              sales_channel_id: salesChannel.id,
              region_id: region.id,
              items: [{ variant_id: kit.variant.id, quantity: 1 }],
            },
            customerHeaders
          )
          .catch((e) => e)

        expect(error.response.status).toEqual(400)
        expect(error.response.data.message).toEqual(
          "Camera kit: Lens is out of stock."
        )
      })

      it("names the variant of an item that isn't a bundle (AC 3)", async () => {
        const lens = await createComponent("Lens", 300, 10)
        const cart = await createCart([{ variant_id: lens.variant.id, quantity: 1 }])

        await setStock(lens.inventoryItem.id, 0)

        const result = await completeCart(cart.id)

        expect(result.error.message).toEqual("Lens is out of stock.")
      })

      it("checks a bundle and a separate line for one of its components together", async () => {
        // One lens in stock: the kit alone or the lens alone would fit, both don't.
        const kit = await createCameraKit({ camera: 10, lens: 1, bag: 10 })
        const cart = await createCart([
          { variant_id: kit.variant.id, quantity: 1 },
          { variant_id: kit.lens.variant.id, quantity: 1 },
        ])

        const result = await completeCart(cart.id).catch((e) => e.response.data)

        expect(result.error.message).toContain("Camera kit: Lens is out of stock.")
        expect(result.error.message).toContain("Lens is out of stock.")
      })
    })

    describe("AC 4: two shoppers buying the last bundle at the same time", () => {
      it("lets one order through and names the component for the other; stock never goes negative", async () => {
        const kit = await createCameraKit({ camera: 1, lens: 1, bag: 1 })

        const cartA = await createCart([{ variant_id: kit.variant.id, quantity: 1 }])
        const cartB = await createCart([{ variant_id: kit.variant.id, quantity: 1 }])

        const results = await Promise.all([
          completeCart(cartA.id),
          completeCart(cartB.id),
        ])

        const orders = results.filter((result) => result.type === "order")
        const failures = results.filter((result) => result.type === "cart")

        expect(orders).toHaveLength(1)
        expect(failures).toHaveLength(1)
        expect(failures[0].error.message).toMatch(
          /^Camera kit: .+ (is|are) out of stock\.$/
        )

        for (const part of [kit.camera, kit.lens, kit.bag]) {
          const level = await getLevel(part.inventoryItem.id)
          expect(level.reserved_quantity).toEqual(1)
          expect(level.stocked_quantity - level.reserved_quantity).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0)
        }
      })
    })

    describe("AC 5: promotions and tax treat a bundle as one line item", () => {
      it("doesn't apply a promotion aimed at a single component to the bundle", async () => {
        const kit = await createCameraKit()

        await api.post(
          "/admin/promotions",
          {
            code: "LENS10",
            type: "standard",
            status: "active",
            application_method: {
              type: "percentage",
              target_type: "items",
              allocation: "each",
              value: 10,
              currency_code: "usd",
              target_rules: [
                {
                  attribute: "items.product.id",
                  operator: "in",
                  values: [kit.lens.product.id],
                },
              ],
            },
          },
          adminHeaders
        )

        const cart = await createCart([{ variant_id: kit.variant.id, quantity: 1 }])
        const updated = (
          await api.post(
            `/store/carts/${cart.id}/promotions`,
            { promo_codes: ["LENS10"] },
            customerHeaders
          )
        ).data.cart

        expect(updated.items).toHaveLength(1)
        expect(updated.items[0].adjustments ?? []).toEqual([])
        expect(updated.items[0].total).toEqual(1000)
      })
    })

    describe("AC 6: fulfilling a bundle ships all of its components", () => {
      it("takes one of each component out of stock", async () => {
        const kit = await createCameraKit()
        const order = await placeOrder(kit.variant.id)

        await fulfillAll(order.id)

        for (const part of [kit.camera, kit.lens, kit.bag]) {
          const level = await getLevel(part.inventoryItem.id)
          expect(level.stocked_quantity).toEqual(9)
          expect(level.reserved_quantity).toEqual(0)
        }
      })
    })

    describe("AC 7-12: refund shares saved when the order is placed", () => {
      it("saves each component's share of the price paid (AC 7, 8, 9)", async () => {
        const kit = await createCameraKit()
        const order = await getOrder((await placeOrder(kit.variant.id)).id)

        expect(order.items[0].metadata.bundle.components).toEqual([
          expect.objectContaining({
            variant_id: kit.camera.variant.id,
            quantity: 1,
            units: 1,
            refund_share: 666.67,
            inventory_items: [
              { inventory_item_id: kit.camera.inventoryItem.id, required_quantity: 1 },
            ],
          }),
          expect.objectContaining({
            variant_id: kit.lens.variant.id,
            refund_share: 250,
          }),
          expect.objectContaining({
            variant_id: kit.bag.variant.id,
            title: "Bag",
            refund_share: 83.33,
          }),
        ])
      })

      it("splits the amount actually paid when the bundle is discounted (AC 10)", async () => {
        const kit = await createCameraKit()

        await api.post(
          "/admin/promotions",
          {
            code: "KIT10",
            type: "standard",
            status: "active",
            application_method: {
              type: "percentage",
              target_type: "items",
              allocation: "each",
              value: 10,
              currency_code: "usd",
              target_rules: [
                {
                  attribute: "items.product.id",
                  operator: "in",
                  values: [kit.bundle.id],
                },
              ],
            },
          },
          adminHeaders
        )

        const cart = await createCart([{ variant_id: kit.variant.id, quantity: 1 }])
        await api.post(
          `/store/carts/${cart.id}/promotions`,
          { promo_codes: ["KIT10"] },
          customerHeaders
        )
        const { order } = await completeCart(cart.id)
        const saved = (await getOrder(order.id)).items[0].metadata.bundle.components

        // $900 paid: 600 / 225 / 75
        expect(saved.map((c) => c.refund_share)).toEqual([600, 225, 75])
      })

      it("keeps the saved shares when prices change later (AC 11)", async () => {
        const kit = await createCameraKit()
        const order = await placeOrder(kit.variant.id)

        await api.post(
          `/admin/products/${kit.lens.product.id}/variants/${kit.lens.variant.id}`,
          { prices: [{ currency_code: "usd", amount: 5000 }] },
          adminHeaders
        )
        await api.post(
          `/admin/bundles/${kit.bundle.id}`,
          { prices: [{ currency_code: "usd", amount: 50 }] },
          adminHeaders
        )

        const saved = (await getOrder(order.id)).items[0].metadata.bundle.components
        expect(saved.map((c) => c.refund_share)).toEqual([666.67, 250, 83.33])
      })

      it("splits by quantity when a component has no price in the order's currency (AC 12)", async () => {
        const kit = await createCameraKit()
        await api.post(
          `/admin/products/${kit.camera.product.id}/variants/${kit.camera.variant.id}`,
          { prices: [{ currency_code: "eur", amount: 800 }] },
          adminHeaders
        )

        const order = await placeOrder(kit.variant.id)
        const saved = (await getOrder(order.id)).items[0].metadata.bundle.components

        expect(saved.map((c) => c.refund_share)).toEqual([333.34, 333.33, 333.33])
      })

      it("doesn't add bundle data to normal lines (AC 21)", async () => {
        const lens = await createComponent("Lens", 300, 10)
        const order = await getOrder((await placeOrder(lens.variant.id)).id)

        expect(order.items[0].metadata?.bundle).toBeUndefined()
      })
    })

    describe("AC 13-21: returning a single item from a bundle", () => {
      let kit
      let order
      let line

      beforeEach(async () => {
        kit = await createCameraKit()
        order = await fulfillAll((await placeOrder(kit.variant.id)).id)
        line = order.items[0]
      })

      it("lets a shopper return just the bag and refunds its share (AC 13, 14)", async () => {
        const before = await pendingDifference(order.id)

        const response = await storeReturn(order.id, [
          { id: line.id, quantity: 1, component_variant_id: kit.bag.variant.id },
        ])

        expect(response.status).toEqual(200)
        expect(response.data.return.items).toEqual([
          expect.objectContaining({
            item_id: line.id,
            quantity: 1,
            metadata: {
              bundle_component: {
                variant_id: kit.bag.variant.id,
                title: "Bag",
                amount: 83.33,
              },
            },
          }),
        ])
        expect((await pendingDifference(order.id)) - before).toBeCloseTo(-83.33, 2)

        // The bundle line itself isn't marked as returned.
        const updated = await getOrder(order.id)
        expect(updated.items[0].detail.return_requested_quantity).toEqual(0)
      })

      it("refunds exactly the bundle price once every item is returned (AC 16)", async () => {
        const before = await pendingDifference(order.id)

        for (const part of [kit.camera, kit.lens, kit.bag]) {
          await storeReturn(order.id, [
            { id: line.id, quantity: 1, component_variant_id: part.variant.id },
          ])
        }

        expect((await pendingDifference(order.id)) - before).toBeCloseTo(-1000, 2)
      })

      it("returns two items of the same bundle in one return", async () => {
        const response = await storeReturn(order.id, [
          { id: line.id, quantity: 1, component_variant_id: kit.lens.variant.id },
          { id: line.id, quantity: 1, component_variant_id: kit.bag.variant.id },
        ])

        expect(response.data.return.items).toHaveLength(2)
      })

      it("restocks only the returned item when the return is received (AC 15)", async () => {
        const { data } = await api.post(
          "/admin/returns",
          { order_id: order.id, location_id: stockLocation.id },
          adminHeaders
        )
        const returnId = data.return.id

        await api.post(
          `/admin/returns/${returnId}/request-items`,
          {
            items: [
              { id: line.id, quantity: 1, component_variant_id: kit.lens.variant.id },
            ],
          },
          adminHeaders
        )
        await api.post(`/admin/returns/${returnId}/request`, {}, adminHeaders)

        await api.post(`/admin/returns/${returnId}/receive`, {}, adminHeaders)
        await api.post(
          `/admin/returns/${returnId}/receive-items`,
          {
            items: [
              { id: line.id, quantity: 1, component_variant_id: kit.lens.variant.id },
            ],
          },
          adminHeaders
        )
        const confirmed = await api.post(
          `/admin/returns/${returnId}/receive/confirm`,
          {},
          adminHeaders
        )
        expect(confirmed.status).toEqual(200)

        expect((await getLevel(kit.lens.inventoryItem.id)).stocked_quantity).toEqual(10)
        expect((await getLevel(kit.camera.inventoryItem.id)).stocked_quantity).toEqual(9)
        expect((await getLevel(kit.bag.inventoryItem.id)).stocked_quantity).toEqual(9)

        const orderReturn = (
          await api.get(`/admin/returns/${returnId}?fields=*items,status`, adminHeaders)
        ).data.return
        expect(orderReturn.status).toEqual("received")
        expect(orderReturn.items).toEqual([
          expect.objectContaining({ quantity: 1, received_quantity: 1 }),
        ])
      })

      it("still returns the whole bundle as one item (AC 17)", async () => {
        const before = await pendingDifference(order.id)

        const response = await storeReturn(order.id, [{ id: line.id, quantity: 1 }])

        expect(response.status).toEqual(200)
        expect((await pendingDifference(order.id)) - before).toBeCloseTo(-1000, 2)
      })

      it("rejects a whole-bundle return after one of its items was returned", async () => {
        await storeReturn(order.id, [
          { id: line.id, quantity: 1, component_variant_id: kit.bag.variant.id },
        ])

        const error = await storeReturn(order.id, [{ id: line.id, quantity: 1 }]).catch(
          (e) => e
        )

        expect(error.response.status).toEqual(400)
        expect(error.response.data.message).toContain("only 0 can be returned whole")
      })

      it("lets an admin refund a different amount than the share (AC 18)", async () => {
        await storeReturn(order.id, [
          { id: line.id, quantity: 1, component_variant_id: kit.bag.variant.id },
        ])

        const payment = (
          await api.get(
            `/admin/orders/${order.id}?fields=*payment_collections.payments`,
            adminHeaders
          )
        ).data.order.payment_collections[0].payments[0]

        await api.post(`/admin/payments/${payment.id}/capture`, {}, adminHeaders)
        const refunded = await api.post(
          `/admin/payments/${payment.id}/refund`,
          { amount: 50 },
          adminHeaders
        )

        expect(refunded.status).toEqual(200)
        expect(refunded.data.payment.refunds).toEqual([
          expect.objectContaining({ amount: 50 }),
        ])
      })

      it("rejects returning more of an item than was bought (AC 19)", async () => {
        const error = await storeReturn(order.id, [
          { id: line.id, quantity: 2, component_variant_id: kit.bag.variant.id },
        ]).catch((e) => e)

        expect(error.response.status).toEqual(400)
        expect(error.response.data.message).toEqual(
          'Cannot return 2 of "Bag" from the bundle "Camera kit": only 1 can be returned.'
        )
      })

      it("rejects returning an item again after it was returned (AC 19)", async () => {
        await storeReturn(order.id, [
          { id: line.id, quantity: 1, component_variant_id: kit.bag.variant.id },
        ])

        const error = await storeReturn(order.id, [
          { id: line.id, quantity: 1, component_variant_id: kit.bag.variant.id },
        ]).catch((e) => e)

        expect(error.response.status).toEqual(400)
        expect(error.response.data.message).toContain("only 0 can be returned")
      })

      it("rejects an item that isn't in that bundle (AC 19)", async () => {
        const other = await createComponent("Tripod", 50, 10)

        const error = await storeReturn(order.id, [
          { id: line.id, quantity: 1, component_variant_id: other.variant.id },
        ]).catch((e) => e)

        expect(error.response.status).toEqual(400)
        expect(error.response.data.message).toEqual(
          `Variant ${other.variant.id} is not part of the bundle "Camera kit".`
        )
      })

      it("only lets the customer who owns the order return a single item (AC 20)", async () => {
        const item = [{ id: line.id, quantity: 1, component_variant_id: kit.bag.variant.id }]

        const guest = await storeReturn(order.id, item, storeHeaders).catch((e) => e)
        expect(guest.response.status).toEqual(401)

        const stranger = await storeReturn(order.id, item, otherCustomerHeaders).catch(
          (e) => e
        )
        expect(stranger.response.status).toEqual(404)

        // Nothing was returned by the rejected requests.
        const owner = await storeReturn(order.id, item)
        expect(owner.status).toEqual(200)
      })
    })
  },
})
```

```text
import {
  ChangeActionType,
  MathBN,
  MedusaError,
} from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import { CreateOrderCreditLineDTO, OrderCreditLineDTO } from "@medusajs/types"
import { OrderChangeProcessing } from "../calculate-order-change"
import { setActionReference } from "../set-action-reference"

OrderChangeProcessing.registerActionType(ChangeActionType.CREDIT_LINE_ADD, {
  operation({ action, currentOrder, options }) {
    const creditLines: (OrderCreditLineDTO | CreateOrderCreditLineDTO)[] =
      currentOrder.credit_lines ?? []
    const existing = creditLines.find(
      (cl) => "id" in cl && cl?.id === action.reference_id
    )

    if (existing) {
      return
    }

    const newCreditLine = {
      order_id: currentOrder.id,
      amount: MathBN.convert(action.amount!),
      reference: action.reference!,
      reference_id: action.reference_id!,
    }

    creditLines.push(newCreditLine)

    setActionReference(newCreditLine, action, options)

    currentOrder.credit_lines = creditLines
  },
  validate({ action }) {
    if (action.amount == null) {
      throw new MedusaError(
        MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
        "Amount is required."
      )
    }
  },
})
```

```bash
cd /workspaces/medusa/packages/modules/order/src/utils && cat >> bundle-component.ts <<'EOF'

/**
 * Records the refund for a received (or dismissed) bundle component as a
 * credit line on the order. Medusa computes the order total from each line's
 * received quantities, which a component return doesn't change, so the credit
 * line is what lowers the total and makes the refund owed to the customer.
 */
export function addBundleComponentCredit(
  currentOrder: { id: string; credit_lines?: any[] },
  action: { id?: string; reference_id?: string; return_id?: string },
  amount: BigNumberInput
) {
  const creditLines = currentOrder.credit_lines ?? []

  creditLines.push({
    order_id: currentOrder.id,
    amount: MathBN.convert(amount),
    reference: "bundle_component_return",
    reference_id: action.return_id ?? action.reference_id,
  })

  currentOrder.credit_lines = creditLines
}
EOF
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**Issue #113 edge case: a cart with a Camera kit plus a separate lens, with only 1 lens in stock, is accepted at checkout (stock oversold). This happens because Medusa's inventory module checks each reservation line on its own, even when two lines use the same item. I fixed it in the inventory module by adding up quantities per item and location within one batch. That fix makes 4 existing inventory-module tests fail, because their fixtures reserve 6 units against a stock of 2. How should I handle it?**

Options:
- **Keep fix, update fixtures (Recommended)** - Keep the inventory module fix and raise the stock in those 4 test fixtures, which only passed because of the bug. Prevents overselling for bundles and for any two cart lines that share an inventory item.
- **Revert, note as tech debt** - Leave Medusa's existing behavior unchanged and list the oversell under Tech Debt in the PR. Smallest change, but a bundle plus one of its components in the same cart can oversell.


**Answer:** Keep fix, update fixtures (Recommended)
</details></tool-use>

```typescript
import {
  ChangeActionType,
  MathBN,
  decorateCartTotals,
} from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import { VirtualOrder } from "@types"
import { calculateOrderChange } from "../../../../utils"

/**
 * Issue #113: returning a single component of a bundle line item. Such an
 * action names the component and its refund in `details.metadata` and must
 * not change the bundle line's own return quantities.
 */
describe("Actions: bundle component returns", function () {
  const order = (): VirtualOrder => ({
    id: "order_1",
    items: [
      {
        id: "item_kit",
        quantity: 1,
        unit_price: 1000,
        compare_at_unit_price: null,
        order_id: "order_1",
        detail: {
          quantity: 1,
          order_id: "order_1",
          delivered_quantity: 1,
          shipped_quantity: 1,
          fulfilled_quantity: 1,
          return_requested_quantity: 0,
          return_received_quantity: 0,
          return_dismissed_quantity: 0,
          written_off_quantity: 0,
        },
      },
    ],
    shipping_methods: [],
    credit_lines: [],
    total: 1000,
  })

  const bag = {
    bundle_component: { variant_id: "bag", title: "Bag", amount: 83.33 },
  }

  const action = (type: ChangeActionType, quantity = 1, metadata = bag) => ({
    action: type,
    return_id: "return_1",
    reference_id: "return_1",
    details: { reference_id: "item_kit", quantity, metadata },
  })

  const detailOf = (result: ReturnType<typeof calculateOrderChange>) =>
    JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(result.order.items[0].detail))

  it("requests a component return without changing the bundle's quantities", function () {
    const result = calculateOrderChange({
      order: order(),
      actions: [action(ChangeActionType.RETURN_ITEM)],
    })

    expect(detailOf(result).return_requested_quantity).toEqual(0)
    expect(result.order.credit_lines).toEqual([])
    // The action's amount is the component's refund, not the bundle price.
    expect(MathBN.convert(result.summary.current_order_total).toNumber()).toEqual(
      1000 - 83.33
    )
  })

  it("adds a credit line for the refund when the component is received", function () {
    const result = calculateOrderChange({
      order: order(),
      actions: [action(ChangeActionType.RECEIVE_RETURN_ITEM)],
    })

    expect(detailOf(result).return_received_quantity).toEqual(0)
    expect(detailOf(result).return_requested_quantity).toEqual(0)
    expect(
      result.order.credit_lines!.map((line: any) => ({
        amount: MathBN.convert(line.amount).toNumber(),
        reference: line.reference,
        reference_id: line.reference_id,
        order_id: line.order_id,
      }))
    ).toEqual([
      {
        amount: 83.33,
        reference: "bundle_component_return",
        reference_id: "return_1",
        order_id: "order_1",
      },
    ])

    // The order total (from line quantities and credit lines) drops by the
    // component's refund, which makes it owed to the customer.
    const totals = decorateCartTotals(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(result.order)))
    expect(MathBN.convert(totals.total).toNumber()).toEqual(916.67)
  })

  it("adds a credit line but doesn't write off quantities when received as damaged", function () {
    const result = calculateOrderChange({
      order: order(),
      actions: [action(ChangeActionType.RECEIVE_DAMAGED_RETURN_ITEM)],
    })

    const detail = detailOf(result)
    expect(detail.return_dismissed_quantity).toEqual(0)
    expect(detail.written_off_quantity).toEqual(0)
    expect(result.order.credit_lines).toHaveLength(1)
  })

  it("cancels a component return without changing the bundle's quantities", function () {
    const result = calculateOrderChange({
      order: order(),
      actions: [action(ChangeActionType.CANCEL_RETURN_ITEM)],
    })

    expect(detailOf(result).return_requested_quantity).toEqual(0)
    expect(result.order.credit_lines).toEqual([])
  })

  it("skips the bundle line's quantity checks for components", function () {
    // The bundle has 0 requested, so receiving 1 whole bundle would fail; the
    // return workflows check component quantities instead.
    expect(() =>
      calculateOrderChange({
        order: order(),
        actions: [action(ChangeActionType.RECEIVE_RETURN_ITEM, 1)],
      })
    ).not.toThrow()

    expect(() =>
      calculateOrderChange({
        order: order(),
        actions: [action(ChangeActionType.RETURN_ITEM, 5)],
      })
    ).not.toThrow()
  })

  it("still checks and counts quantities for whole-bundle returns", function () {
    expect(() =>
      calculateOrderChange({
        order: order(),
        actions: [action(ChangeActionType.RECEIVE_RETURN_ITEM, 1, {} as any)],
      })
    ).toThrow(
      "Cannot receive more items than what was requested to be returned for item item_kit."
    )

    const result = calculateOrderChange({
      order: order(),
      actions: [action(ChangeActionType.RETURN_ITEM, 1, {} as any)],
    })
    expect(detailOf(result).return_requested_quantity).toEqual(1)
  })
})
```

```text
# Mutation testing: Issue #62 -- Add a Low-Stock Inventory Monitoring Dashboard

**PR(s):** [#115](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/medusa/pull/115)  **Tool:** StrykerJS 10.1.1 with the Jest runner (`@stryker-mutator/core`, `@stryker-mutator/jest-runner`)  **Config:** [stryker.config.json](../../../packages/modules/inventory/stryker.config.json) and its build step [stryker-build.cjs](../../../packages/modules/inventory/stryker-build.cjs) (my own setup; no teammate setup existed)  **Command:** `cd packages/modules/inventory && npx stryker run` (Postgres running)
**Reports:** [before](reports/62-njpiombino-before.json) · [after](reports/62-njpiombino-after.json)
**Mutation score:** before 77.78% (56 of 72 killed) → after 84.72% (61 of 72 killed)

**Scope.** Mutated: the 111 lines that #62 added to `packages/modules/inventory/src/services/inventory-module.ts` (lines 443-553: the `stock_status` handling in `listInventoryItems` / `listAndCountInventoryItems` and the SQL helper `listIdsByStockStatus_`). That is where all of the PR's filtering, sorting and paging logic lives. Not mutated:
- the type files, which have no runtime code;
- `validators.ts`, a two-value zod enum covered only by the HTTP suite, which boots a full server against built packages;
- the dashboard files, which are tested with Vitest, not Jest.

Tests run: `packages/modules/inventory/integration-tests/__tests__/inventory-module-service.spec.ts` (44 tests before, 48 after).

**Setup problems solved:**
- The module tests load `dist/`, not `src/`. The config therefore rebuilds the package after Stryker instruments the file (`buildCommand`), and runs `inPlace` because the sandbox copy breaks the package tsconfig's relative `extends`.
- Babel, which Stryker uses to instrument the file, drops parameter decorators on parameters with a default value. Every `@MedusaContext() context: Context = {}` lost its decorator, so 8 existing tests failed in the initial run. This happens in both Babel 8 (Stryker 10) and Babel 7.29 (Stryker 9). `stryker-build.cjs` restores the 35 decorators before building.
- `moduleIntegrationTestRunner` wraps suites in `describe("")`, so Stryker's per-test coverage IDs never match Jest's test names, and every mutant was reported as uncovered. `coverageAnalysis` is set to `all`, so every test runs against every mutant.
- `concurrency` is 1 because every test run uses the same test database name.

## Surviving mutants

All 16 mutants that were not killed in the before run (13 survived, 3 had no coverage). Line numbers are in `packages/modules/inventory/src/services/inventory-module.ts`. The source file is identical in both reports.

| Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| inventory-module.ts:450 (#3) | `!filters.stock_status` → `false` in `listInventoryItems` | Equivalent | `listInventoryItems` then always calls `listAndCountInventoryItems`, which runs the same check and returns the same items without the filter. Only an extra count query is added. |
| inventory-module.ts:450 (#4) | early-return block → `{}` | Equivalent | Falls through to the same `listAndCountInventoryItems` path as #3. |
| inventory-module.ts:476 (#12) | `!sortedIds.length` → `false` | Equivalent | With no ids, the intersection query gets `id: []`, which matches nothing, so the result is still `[[], 0]`. The early return only saves two queries. |
| inventory-module.ts:476 (#13) | early-return block → `{}` | Equivalent (no coverage before, survived after) | Same reasoning as #12: falling through produces `[[], 0]`. |
| inventory-module.ts:477 (#14) | `return [[], 0]` → `return []` | Test gap, **killed after** | No test had zero items with the status in the database, so the early return never ran. A caller destructuring `[items, count]` would get `undefined`. |
| inventory-module.ts:477 (#15) | `[]` → `["Stryker was here"]` | Test gap, **killed after** | Same gap as #14: would return a fake item. |
| inventory-module.ts:482 (#18) | `{ id: sortedIds }` → `{}` in the intersection query | Equivalent | The next line filters to `sortedIds` again in memory, so narrowing in SQL only reduces rows read. |
| inventory-module.ts:483 (#19) | `{ select: ["id"] }` → `{}` | Equivalent | Only `id` is read from the result. Selecting all fields gives the same ids. |
| inventory-module.ts:483 (#20) | `["id"]` → `[]` | Equivalent | An empty select loads default fields, which include `id`. |
| inventory-module.ts:483 (#21) | `"id"` → `""` | Equivalent | The query still returns the primary key, the only field used. |
| inventory-module.ts:492 (#27) | `config.take == null` → `true` (ignore `take`) | Test gap, **killed after** | The only paging test used `skip: 1, take: 1` with 2 matches, which returns 1 item even when `take` is ignored. No test limited the first page. |
| inventory-module.ts:494 (#33) | `!pageIds.length` → `false` | Equivalent | Fetching `id: []` returns no items, so the result is `[[], count]` either way. |
| inventory-module.ts:494 (#34) | early-return block → `{}` | Equivalent | Same as #33. |
| inventory-module.ts:499 (#37) | `{ id: pageIds }` → `{}` for the page fetch | Equivalent | The page is rebuilt from `pageIds` through a map, so extra rows are ignored. Only a performance difference. |
| inventory-module.ts:500 (#38) | config `{ ...config, skip, take, order }` → `{}` | Test gap, **killed after** | Dropping the caller's `select` / `relations` was not detected because the module tests only compared ids. The API depends on the requested fields being returned. |
| inventory-module.ts:531 (#57) | `join(", ")` → `join("")` in the error message | Test gap, **killed after** | The tests only passed one invalid status, so the separator never appeared in the message. |

## New or strengthened test

Commit: [3c1a11d](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/medusa/commit/3c1a11d98eb2d48eed7a56c2e90160d9b2e098ba) · Tests, all in `packages/modules/inventory/integration-tests/__tests__/inventory-module-service.spec.ts`:
- `Inventory Module Service › stock_status filter › limits the first page to take` kills #27 (inventory-module.ts:492).
- `› stock_status filter › keeps the requested relations` kills #38 (inventory-module.ts:500).
- `› stock_status filter without matching items › returns nothing when no item has the status` kills #14 and #15 (inventory-module.ts:477).
- `› stock_status filter › names every unknown stock status` kills #57 (inventory-module.ts:531).

All five show as `Killed` in the after report.

## Questions

1. **What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?** Most survivors (11 of 16) were equivalent. They remove shortcuts such as early returns and narrower queries that only save database work, which no test can observe through results. The five real gaps were all edge cases at the boundaries of the paging code:
   - a first page limited by `take`;
   - the case where nothing in the database has the status;
   - the caller's `relations` / `select` being passed through;
   - more than one invalid value.

   The tests checked the main behaviour (which items, in what order, how many) well. They did not check that the filter leaves the rest of the list contract (paging and requested fields) intact.

2. **Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements?** Yes, partly. #57 is in the error message text, and the expected messages in "rejects an unknown stock status" and "names every unknown stock status" come from wording I chose in the code, not from the issue. The issue only implies that invalid input should be rejected; the HTTP test checks the requirement-level behaviour (a 400 error). The other expected values (which items are low or out of stock, the sort order, counts, an empty result) come from the acceptance criteria, the threshold rule agreed in #61, and the sort order agreed in the #62 discussion.

3. **AI use.** Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) did the following:
   - installed and configured StrykerJS;
   - found and worked around the three setup problems above: the module tests load `dist/`, Babel drops parameter decorators (located by capturing the instrumented file during a dry run and reproducing it with Babel directly), and the `describe("")` coverage-ID mismatch;
   - wrote the module-level `stock_status` tests;
   - classified each survivor;
   - wrote the four tests that kill the gap survivors.

   What was verified:
   - The baseline run passed all tests before mutation.
   - After each Stryker run, the source file was checked to contain no instrumentation.
   - The scores in this doc were recomputed from the committed JSON reports.
   - The equivalence claims were checked by reading the code paths described in the table.

   Verified by me: I reran `npx stryker run` myself with this config, and I reviewed this whole document: the setup notes, every row of the surviving-mutants table, the new tests and the answers above. I also checked the feature manually in the admin inventory page.
```

```bash
import itertools, functools
def run(weights,total,mut):
    W=sum(weights); shares=[total*w//W for w in weights]
    if mut==168: rem=[total*w+shares[i]*W for i,w in enumerate(weights)]
    elif mut==170: rem=[total*w-shares[i]//W for i,w in enumerate(weights)]  # bigint div
    else: rem=[total*w-shares[i]*W for i,w in enumerate(weights)]
    idx=list(range(len(weights)))
    def cmp(a,b):
        ra,rb=rem[a],rem[b]
        if mut==178:
            return -1 if ra>rb else 1
        if ra==rb:
            return (a+b) if mut==180 else (a-b)
        return -1 if ra>rb else 1
    idx.sort(key=functools.cmp_to_key(cmp))
    left=total-sum(shares)
    for i in idx:
        if left<=0: break
        shares[i]+=1; left-=1
    return shares
found={}
for n in (2,3,4):
  for weights in itertools.product(range(1,7),repeat=n):
    for total in range(1,15):
      base=run(list(weights),total,0)
      for m in (168,170,178,180):
        if m not in found and run(list(weights),total,m)!=base:
          found[m]=(weights,total,base,run(list(weights),total,m))
print(found)
EOF
python3 rem.py
```

```bash
import re
def remove_tests(s, titles):
    L=s.split('\n'); out=[]; i=0; removed=set()
    while i<len(L):
        line=L[i]; m=re.match(r'^(\s*)it\(\s*$', line) or re.match(r'^(\s*)it\("(.*?)",', line)
        hit=None
        for t in titles:
            if f'it("{t}"' in line or (line.strip()=='it(' and i+1<len(L) and f'"{t}"' in L[i+1]):
                hit=t
        if hit:
            ind=line[:len(line)-len(line.lstrip())]
            j=i+1
            while not (L[j]==ind+'})' ): j+=1
            i=j+1
            if i<len(L) and L[i].strip()=='': i+=1
            removed.add(hit); continue
        out.append(line); i+=1
    missing=set(titles)-removed
    assert not missing, missing
    return '\n'.join(out)
```

```markdown
## Questions

1. **What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?** The tests covered the issue's main example well: one Camera kit with one of each item, returned one item at a time. Most gaps (26 of 37) came from inputs outside that example:
   - a bundle holding several of one component (#244, #308);
   - a free component next to priced ones (#154);
   - rounding where the larger share and the larger remainder differ (#168, #170);
   - a whole-bundle return combined with single items in one request, or after earlier returns (#272, #280, #282, #283);
   - the same item returned from two order lines, or a whole bundle and an item of the same line in one return (#336, #340);
   - receiving the same item twice in one request (#360, #361);
   - data shapes the tests never built: `null` metadata, a bundle ordered before shares were saved, a product without its variant list (#249, #268, #13).

   Several of these would have crashed or refunded the wrong amount. The other gap was in the mocked query: the unit tests didn't check which fields the error message loads (#88-#94, #114). The HTTP suite covers that against a real database, but Stryker can't run it. The 11 equivalent survivors are internal key text, sort tie-breaking that a stable sort already handles, and data states the code never writes.

2. **Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements?** Yes, in three places:
   - #280 is in the error message, and the expected messages ("only 1 can be returned whole …", "Cannot return 2 of "Bag" …") use wording I chose; the issue only says a request must be rejected with a clear error.
   - The query fields asserted for #88-#94 come from what the code needs to build a name, not from the issue.
   - The rounding tests for #168 and #170 use the largest-remainder rule (the earlier component wins a tie). The issue only asks that leftover cents go to "specific components chosen by a fixed rule"; the rule itself is my choice, recorded in the PR's design decisions.

   The other expected values come from the requirements: the shares 666.67 / 250 / 83.33 from the owner's example (the bag is 1/12 of the kit), shares adding up exactly to the price paid (AC 9), splitting by quantity when a price is missing (AC 12), rejecting more than was bought (AC 19), and whole-bundle returns still working for older orders (AC 19).

3. **AI use.** Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) did the following:
   - wrote the Stryker config for this package, starting from my #62 setup, and found that the sandbox copy breaks the relative require in `jest.config.js` (fixed with `inPlace`);
   - ran both passes, classified every survivor, and wrote the 14 new tests and the strengthened one;
   - for #168 and #170, searched small inputs with a script to find a case that tells the real rounding apart from the mutants, and checked the expected shares by hand (0.02 split 1:2 gives exact shares of 0.0067 and 0.0133, and the cent goes to the larger remainder);
   - argued the equivalence of the tie-break mutants from how a stable sort uses its comparator. The same search found no input on which they differ.

   What was verified:
   - Both runs were made on the same, formatted source, and the reports' embedded source matches the committed files.
   - The scores in this doc were recomputed from the committed JSON reports.
   - The "before" run used the test files with only the 14 new tests removed and the strengthened assertion restored to its earlier, weaker form.
   - After each run, both files were checked to contain no instrumentation (`stryNS`).
```

````markdown
## Summary

**What** — What changes are introduced in this PR?

Part 2 of product bundles (#101): bundles now work from checkout through returns.

- Out-of-stock errors name the product, for example "Camera kit: Lens is out of stock." (at add-to-cart and at checkout).
- When an order is placed, each bundle item's share of the price paid is saved on the order line.
- A shopper (store API) or admin can return a single item from a bundle. The refund is that item's share, and only that item goes back into stock.
- Checkout no longer oversells when two cart lines use the same stock (a bundle plus one of its items).

**Why** — Why are these changes relevant or necessary?

Closes #113. Shoppers need to know which item stopped their order, and store owners asked to accept returns of single bundle items with a fair, predictable refund.

**How** — How have these changes been implemented?

- Checkout: `confirmInventoryStep` (add-to-cart) and `reserveInventoryStep` (checkout) build their error with `insufficient-inventory-error.ts`, which resolves a short inventory item to the bundle item that uses it. The inventory module now checks stock per item and location across all lines of a reservation batch.
- Shares: a new `prepareBundleRefundSharesStep` in `completeCartWorkflow` splits the bundle line's total (after discounts, including tax) by each item's normal price and saves the result in the order line's `metadata.bundle`. The maths is in `bundle-refunds.ts`.
- Returns: return items accept `component_variant_id`. New steps `prepareBundleReturnItemsStep` and `prepareBundleReceiveItemsStep` validate the request and record the item and its refund in the return item's metadata. They're wired into the store return, admin request, receive, dismiss and confirm-receive workflows. The order module's return actions leave the bundle line's own quantities alone for these items, and on receipt add a credit line for the refund. Confirming receipt restocks only the item's inventory.
- Store API: `POST /store/returns` accepts an optional customer login. Returning a single bundle item requires the logged-in customer who owns the order.
- A changeset is included (patch).

**Testing** — How have these changes been tested, or how can the reviewer test the feature?

See Test Evidence below. To try it: create a bundle (`POST /admin/bundles`), buy it, fulfill it, then `POST /store/returns` with `component_variant_id` as the order's customer.

---

## Examples

```ts
// Checkout when the lens sold out
POST /store/carts/:id/complete
// 200 { type: "cart", error: { message: "Camera kit: Lens is out of stock.", type: "not_allowed" } }

// Saved on the order line (kit sold for $1,000; camera/lens/bag normally $800/$300/$100)
order.items[0].metadata.bundle.components
// [{ variant_id: "variant_camera", refund_share: 666.67, units: 1, ... },
//  { variant_id: "variant_lens",   refund_share: 250,    ... },
//  { variant_id: "variant_bag",    refund_share: 83.33,  ... }]

// Return only the bag (logged-in customer who owns the order)
POST /store/returns
{
  "order_id": "order_123",
  "items": [{ "id": "ordli_kit", "quantity": 1, "component_variant_id": "variant_bag" }],
  "return_shipping": { "option_id": "so_return" },
  "receive_now": true
}
// return.items[0].metadata.bundle_component = { variant_id: "variant_bag", title: "Bag", amount: 83.33 }
// The order's pending difference drops by 83.33; one bag goes back into stock.
```

---

## Design

**Decision:** A single-item return is a normal return line on the bundle's order line, with the returned item and its refund in the line's metadata. The refund is booked as an order credit line when the item is received.

**Alternatives considered:**
- Count the bag as 1/12 of a bundle (fractional quantity on the bundle line). Rejected: admins would see fractional quantities, the maths needs extra rounding, and restocking would still need custom code.
- Replace the bundle line with one line per item before the return ("unbundle"), then use the normal return flow. Rejected: it rewrites order and fulfillment history, which is risky for past orders.
- Use the return action's amount for the refund. Tried first: Medusa recalculates the saved order total from each line's returned quantities, not from action amounts, so the refund never showed. The credit line is the mechanism Medusa already uses to lower an order's total.

**Rationale:** It uses Medusa's existing extension points (metadata on return items and actions, credit lines), keeps order history intact, and needs no data migration.

**Consequences:**
- A returned item shows up as a credit line (`reference: "bundle_component_return"`) rather than as a returned quantity on the bundle line.
- The bundle line isn't marked as returned even when all its items are; the return items show what came back.
- Exchanges and claims don't support single bundle items.

**Other decisions:**
- **What is split:** the bundle line's total after discounts and including tax, so returning every item refunds exactly what was paid (AC 7, 10). Rejected: the subtotal before tax with tax refunded separately (more code, and the sum wouldn't equal what was paid).
- **Rounding:** each share is rounded down to the currency's smallest unit, and leftover cents go one each to the largest remainders, with the earlier item winning a tie. Partial returns spread a share by rounding the running total down, so they always add up to it (AC 9, 16). Rejected: rounding each share to nearest (doesn't always add up), and giving all leftover cents to the first item (less fair).
- **Missing price:** if an item has no price in the order's currency, the whole line is split by quantity (AC 12). Rejected: blocking the sale, and splitting only the unpriced item by quantity.
- **Older orders:** a single-item return from an order placed before shares were saved is rejected; returning the whole bundle still works (AC 19). Rejected: working shares out from today's prices (the refund would depend on later price changes).
- **Store login (owner-approved):** only single bundle item returns require the logged-in customer who owns the order. Guest returns of normal items and whole bundles work as before. Rejected: requiring login for all store returns (breaks guest returns), and leaving it open.
- **Whole bundle after a single item:** a whole-bundle return is only allowed for bundles none of whose items were returned. Rejected: allowing it (refunds the returned item twice).
- **Out-of-stock wording:** the error names the bundle and the item ("Camera kit: Lens is out of stock."); other products are named on their own ("T-shirt (L) is out of stock."). The error type and code are unchanged, so clients that check `INSUFFICIENT_INVENTORY` still work. Rejected: naming only the item (the shopper sees the kit in their cart), and keeping the generic message for non-bundles (AC 3).
- **Oversell fix in the inventory module (owner-approved):** stock is checked per item and location across all lines of a batch. Rejected: a pre-check in core-flows (an extra query on every checkout), and leaving it as tech debt.

---

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- Single-item returns are validated in a workflow step without a lock, so two simultaneous requests for the same item could both pass. Normal returns are checked inside the order module's transaction.
- The quantity of a requested or received single item can't be edited in place. The admin removes it and adds it again (the update workflows return a clear error).
- An admin can still send arbitrary metadata on exchange and claim items, which these changes don't validate. Return items are cleaned.

**Encountered:**
- `POST /store/returns` had no login check: anyone with an order ID can create a return. This is only closed for single bundle items (see Design).
- The inventory module checked each reservation line on its own, so two lines using the same stock could oversell. Fixed here; 4 existing inventory-module test fixtures reserved 6 units against a stock of 2 and were updated.
- `createAndCompleteReturnOrderWorkflow` with `receive_now` received every item of the order instead of the returned ones. It now receives the returned items.
````

**What it does**
- **Checkout errors:** the out-of-stock error now names the bundle and the item, for example "Camera kit: Lens is out of stock." It works both when adding to the cart and at checkout. Products that aren't bundles are named too, for example "T-shirt (L) is out of stock."

- **Store login:** returning a single bundle item through the store needs the logged-in customer who owns the order, as you chose. Guest returns work as before.

**Two things I found along the way**
- **Refunds:** Medusa ignores a return's own refund amount when it recalculates the order total, so a single-item refund never showed up. The refund is now recorded as a credit line on the order, which is the mechanism Medusa already uses to lower an order's total.
